texts.preamble: Urmila Thakur vs Anita And Ors on 11 February, 2026 In The Court Of Ms. Pragati, Senior Civil Judge-Cum- Rent Controller, Karkardooma Courts, Shahdara Rc Arc 55/2022 Case Registration no. Dlsh03-000283-2022 Urmila Thakur, W/o Sh. Puran Singh, R/o 9/2888, Gurudwara Gali, Kailash Nagar, Gandhi Nagar, Delhi-110031.
texts.facts: (hereinafter referred to as the "tenanted premises"). That the petitioner purchased the tenanted premises by virtue of registered sale deed dated 04.08.2006 executed by Smt. Renu Jain, Sh. Rajesh Jain, Sh. Rakesh Kumar and Sh. Vimal Jain in favour of petitioner. That one Lt. Sh. Hari Chand was a tenant in the tenanted premises prior to purchase of the tenanted premises by the petitioner and after the death of Sh. Hari Chand, the tenancy was inherited by only one of his legal heirs / son i.e. Sh. Veer Singh Thakur and he had lastly paid rent of Rs.400/- in respect of tenanted premises on 31.08.2009. Thus, there is no relationship of landlord and tenant between the petitioner and the other legal heirs of Lt. Sh. Hari Chand. That the respondent no.4 (one of the sons of Lt. Sh. Hari Chand) never remained in use and occupation of the tenanted premises, however, he wanted to grab the same in one way or the other. That Sh. Veer Singh expired leaving behind his legal heirs i.e. Smt. Anita (wife), Sh. Shelly (son) and Ms. Pooja (daughter) i.e. respondent no.1, respondent no.2 and respondent no.3 respectively but the tenanted premises was illegally sublet by the original tenant to respondent no.5, signed by PRAGATI PRAGATI Date: 2026.02.11 18:29:57 +0530 who is running his shop under the name and style of M/s. Muradabadi Chicken Biriyani Center in the tenanted premises without any consent of the petitioner, therefore, respondents are liable to be evicted therefrom. Hence, the present petition. 3) Summons of the present petition were served upon the respondents no.4 and 5 on 10.03.2022 and written statement was filed on behalf of respondent no.4. Summons were served upon the respondents no.1 to 3 by way of publication on 07.10.2022, however, none had appeared on behalf of the respondents no.1 to 3 and 5 before the court therefore, vide order dated 13.10.2022 and 07.12.2022, respectively, the respondents no. 1 to 3 and respondent no.5 respectively were proceeded against ex-parte. 4) Written statement filed on behalf of respondent no.4:- It is stated by respondent no.4 that he is a tenant in the tenanted premises at a monthly rent of Rs.100/- not at a monthly rent of Rs.400/- as alleged by the petitioner. That the petitioner has filed forged and fabricated rent receipts showing the rent of Rs.400/- p.m. That respondent no.4 is running his shop in the tenanted premises and has not sublet the same to anyone. That the respondent no.4 had filed DR petition bearing no.58/2016 before the court for deposition of rent and therein the petitioner had filed his objections and the same were dismissed and the petitioner was directed to provide his account details to the respondent no.4 so that the rent may be deposited but the petitioner did not provide the account details and has been receiving the rent without issuing rent receipt. That the petition of the petitioner is bad for misjoinder and non-joinder of parties. That respondents no.1 to 3 or Lt. Sh. Veer Singh have never Urmila Thakur vs Anita And Ors on 11 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/158623517/ 2 been in possession of the tenanted premises nor they ever paid the rent to the petitioner. That respondent no.5 has no concern with the tenanted premises and he is the employee on daily Digitally signed by PRAGATI PRAGATI Date: 2026.02.11 18:30:01 +0530 wages of respondent no.4. That respondent no.4 is running the business of property dealing in the tenanted premises and there has not been any sub- letting of the tenanted premises. Thus, it is prayed that the present petition may be dismissed. 5) Replication qua the written statement filed on behalf of the respondent no.4:- Replication was filed on behalf of the petitioner, denying therein the allegations/averments of the respondent no.4. Further, the contents of the petition were reiterated. In order to substantiate her case, the petitioner got examined PW1 i.e. Sh. S.P. Singh, designated officer/Licencing Authority, Department of Food Safety, Govt. of NCT Delhi (i.e. summoned witness) who brought the summoned record i.e., S.no Documents Exhibit/mark 1. Certified copy of complete records Ex.PW1/1 (colly) pertaining to certificate bearing no.2332100902122 issued on 20.02.2021 to the respondent no.5 by the Dept. of Food Safety, Govt. of NCT Delhi 2. Certificate bearing no. 2332100902122 Ex.PW1/2 7) Further, the petitioner also got examined herself as PW2 and tendered in her examination-in-chief, her affidavit as Ex.PW2/A wherein she reiterated the contents of the petition. She further led into evidence the following documents:- PRAGATI Date: S.no. Documents Exhi 2. Photocopy of sale deed dated Ex.PW2/2 04.08.2006 3. Photocopy of rent receipt Ex.PW 4. Photocopy of objections/reply filed Ex.PW2/4 (OSR) by the petitioner in DR petition bearing no 452/2012 titled as Rajesh@Raju v. Smt. Urmila 5. Photocopy of order dated Ex.PW2/5 (OSR) Registration certificate issued by Ex.PW1/2 FSSAI to the respondent no.5 13. Photographs of tenanted premises Ex.PW2/12 14. Newspaper dated 27.01.2022 Ex.PW2/13 8) In her cross-examination, she could not recall as to whether any notice was issued to Sh. Rajesh Kumar. She volunteered that Rajesh Kumar is not their tenant. On being confronted with the reply dated 14.09.2012, she stated that she does not remember whether this reply was given by her in response to the notice. She admitted that Sh. Gauri Shankar Mathur was previously engaged by her. She further admitted that she had filed RCA no.18/13 and she had filed the notice dated 08.08.2012 (Ex. PW 2/RX1) issued by respondent and reply dated 14.09.2012 (PW2/RX2). Further, she stated that previously, Sh. Hari Chand was a tenant in the suit property but he had died in the year 2000 and the landlady was Lt. Smt. Renu Jain. She Digitally signed by PRAGATI PRAGATI Date: 2026.02.11 18:30:11 expressed her ignorance as to whether Smt. Renu Jain used to receive the rent @Rs.100/- per month from the respondent against receipt issued by her in the name of Sh. Hari Chand. She stated that she has never given any notice to the legal heirs of Sh. Hari Chand. She admitted that Sh. Rajesh @ Raju (respondent no.4), is the son of Sh. Hari Chand. That she does not know anything about the Urmila Thakur vs Anita And Ors on 11 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/158623517/ 4 litigation between her and respondent no.4, only her husband used to deal with the same. That she does not know how many sons and daughters Sh. Hari Chand is having. She stated that she received the rent from Sh. Veer Singh from 2006 to 2009. She denied that Sh. Veer Singh was never the tenant in the tenanted premises nor he was paying any rent to her. She further denied that Sh. Veer Singh was never in occupation of the tenanted premises or he ran the shop. She denied that Sh. Hari Chand alongwith Sh. Rajesh was running the shop and after the death of Sh. Hari Chand, Sh. Rajesh used to run the shop and pay the rent @ Rs.100/- per month. She stated that the previous owner from whom she purchased the tenanted premises had told her that Sh. Hari Chand was a tenant therein. She stated that she does not remember whether the rent receipts/counter foil issued by the previous owner to Sh. Hari Chand was handed over to her when she purchased the tenanted premises. She stated that she is an illiterate person. That she does not remember as to whether she had issued any notice for increase the rent from Rs.100/- to further. That her husband used to issue rent receipts which were signed by her. She denied that Sh. Veer Singh was never a tenant and she has fabricated rent receipts in collusion with her husband. She denied that Sh. Rajesh is a tenant in the tenanted premises or is doing work of property and selling biryani. She volunteered that Anita, Pooja and Shelly have handed over the possession of the tenanted premises to Riyasat and he is doing the work of selling biryani. She denied that Anita, Pooja and Shelly were not tenants in the tenanted premises or have handed over the possession of the tenanted Digitally signed by PRAGATI PRAGATI Date: 2026.02.11 18:30:15 +0530 premises to Riyasat where he is doing the work of selling biryani. She stated that she does not know whether Riyasat is the workman of Sh. Rajesh. She denied that the documents Ex.PW2/3 do not bear signatures of Sh. Veer Singh and his signatures have been forged by her. She denied that Sh. Rajesh @ Raju has not sublet the suit property to Riyasat. She denied that no person other than Sh. Rajesh have been a tenant in the suit property. She stated that she did not take any action for eviction of Sh. Rajesh because he was never in occupation of the tenanted premises. She denied that Sh. Rajesh has been in possession of the tenanted premises since beginning. She denied that the photographs placed on record by her in respect of the tenanted premises are forged documents. She denied that Ex.PW1/2 has been created by them to create a false evidence. She denied that she has filed a false petition and false affidavit of evidence. 9) No other witness was examined by the petitioner. The petitioner evidence was closed by way of a separate statement of petitioner dated 06.07.2023. 10) Respondent No.4's Evidence:- Thereafter, the respondent no.4 was granted the opportunity to lead his evidence wherein he got examined himself as RW4 and tendered in his examination-in-chief, his affidavit as Ex.RW4/A wherein he reiterated the contents of the written statement. He further led into evidence the following documents:- Urmila Thakur vs Anita And Ors on 11 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/158623517/ 5 S.no. Documents Exhibit/Mark 1. Photocopy of agreement between Ex.RW4/1 (OSR) respondent no.5 and respondent no.4 dated 17.03.2020 2. Photocopy of affidavit of respondent Ex.RW4/2 (OSR) no.5 dated 31.01.2022 objected to on the PRAGATI 2026.02.11 ground of mode or proof 3. Photocopy of license of Rajesh Ex.RW4/3 (OSR). Kumar/respondent no.4 Objected to on the grond of mode of pro for lack of certific u/s 65B of Indian Evidence Act 11) In his cross-examination, he stated that he has studied till class tenth. He stated that he cannot read English but he can understand little bit of english. That he is aware of the contents of his affidavit Ex.RW4/A. That his advocate explained the contents of the is affidavit. He stated that he had told his advocate what is to be written in his affidavit. He stated that Lt. Sh. Hari Chand is his father. That at the time when the petitioner purchased the property no.IX/2399, Gali no.14, Main Road, Kailash Nagar, Delhi, he alongwith his father was a tenant at the tenanted premises. He again said that at that time, his father had already expired and only he was the tenant in the tenanted premises. That he is not aware whether the property no. IX/2399, Gali no.14, Main Road, Kailash Nagar, Delhi was purchased by the petitioner vide registered sale deed dated 04.08.2006. That in the year 2006, he was working as a property dealer by the name of Hari Chand Property Dealers at property no. IX/2399, Gali no.14, Main Road, Kailash Nagar, Delhi and he continues till date to work as a property dealer from the same address. He stated that he can produce the documents which show that he has been working as a property dealer from the year 2006 till date from the said address of property no. IX/2399, Gali no.14, Main Road, Kailash Nagar, Delhi. He stated that he had shown his documents regarding his property dealing business being run from the said address from the year 2006 till date to his counsel at the time of filing of his written statement in the present case. However, he has not placed on record Digitally signed by PRAGATI PRAGATI Date: 2026.02.11 18:30:23 +0530 any document to show that he is in possession of the tenanted premises from the year 2006 till date. He volunteered that he can produce the documents. He further stated that no one came to take the rent from him. He volunteered that he had not gone personally to give the rent to the petitioner and he had got the rent sent to the petitioner through the court. That he had not personally sent the rent to the petitioner. He volunteered that he did not know who the landlord is and when he came to know the name of the landlord he filed the court case for deposit of the rent. That the landlord of the tenanted premises is Smt. Urmila Devi. That he does not Urmila Thakur vs Anita And Ors on 11 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/158623517/ 6 remember the year when he came to know that Smt. Urmila Devi is the landlord of the tenanted premises. That he had got the court case for deposit of rent filed in the name of Smt. Urmila Devi. He had personally met Smt. Urmila Devi. He volunteered that Smt. Urmila Devi is his distant relative). He stated that he has known Smt.Urmila Devi since he was a child. That he has never seen any document such as Voter Card, Aadhar Card, Ration Card or any similar document mentioning the name of Smt. Urmila Devi. That he came to know the name of the petitioner when he came to know that she has purchased the property no. IX/2399, Gali no.14, Main Road, Kailash Nagar, Delhi. He stated that his father Lt. Sh. Hari Chand expired in the year 2000, however, he does not know the date and month. On being confronted with the No Objection Certificate dated 15.09.2021 issued by Lt. Sh. Hari Chand (part of Ex.PW1/1 (colly)) he stated that the signatures at point X in the said document is not of his father. He volunteered that his father did not know English and he used to sign in Hindi. He stated that he has not filed any document in which his father's signature is made in Hindi. He volunteered that he can produce the document in this regard. On seeing photographs PRAGATI 2026.02.11 Ex.PW2/12, he stated that one photograph (Mark X), on which the board of Hari Chand Property Dealer is visible, is of the tenanted premises. Further, he stated that he is unable to identify the tenanted premises in the remaining photographs as most of the shops in that area look similar. He further stated that he does not know the person at point XI sitting inside the shop in the photograph Mark X. Again he said, he is unable to see clearly the face of the said person as the same is not visible. He could not recall as to whether he has any license for running property dealer business in his name in the tenanted premises. He volunteered that there was some document of the market association in the name of his father and since it is a very old document, he will have to trace the same and can produce before the court. He further stated that he has got mentioned in his written statement and his affidavit of evidence Ex.RW4/A that he has been working as a property dealer at the tenanted premises. He denied that he has not mentioned the same. Further, he stated that he cannot identify the signatures at points X in the receipts ex. PW 2/3. That the said receipts are not of his brother. He volunteered that the said receipts appear to be false. That Sh. Veer Singh is his elder brother and he expired in the year 2008. He volunteered that he does not remember the exact date/month/year of the death of his brother. That his elder brother had several occupations during his lifetime such as property dealer, seller of chicken biryani. He volunteered that he had not contact with his elder brother Sh. Veer Singh and their relationship was strained. He admitted that the respondent no.1 is the wife of Sh. Veer Singh and the respondent no.2 and 3 are the son and daughter of Sh. Veer Singh. He denied that Sh. Veer Singh was in use and occupation of the tenanted premises when the same was purchased by the petitioner. He volunteered that Sh. Veer Singh never visited or sat at the tenanted premises during his lifetime. That earlier he did not have knowledge that Sh. Veer Singh used PRAGATI 2026.02.11 to pay rent to the petitioner in respect of tenanted Urmila Thakur vs Anita And Ors on 11 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/158623517/ 7 premises, he came to know of the same when the receipts were filed in the present case. That he did not file any complaint to the police or any court case or issued any notice to the petitioner that the said receipts were forged, after filing of the present case. Again said, when he was doing property dealing work, Sh. Sunil Babbar used to be his employee at the tenanted premises and now he is selling chicken biryani at the tenanted premises and he has engaged two employees Sh. Riyasat and Sh. Firasat. That he executed the agreement Ex. RW 4/1 and affidavit Ex. RW 4/2 with respondent No.5/Riyasat because he is a labourer and he may not grab the tenanted premises. He paid labour @ Rs. 500/- per day to Riyasat. Riyasat has been working with him since the year 2000. That he does not make any payment to the two employees that Riyasat Urmila Thakur vs Anita And Ors on 11 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/158623517/ 8 has kept and he does not know the payment that is being made by Riyasat to the said two employees. That he has brought the documents to show that he has been in possession of the tenanted premises from the date of the filing of present case till date:- S.no. Documents Exhibit/Mark 1. Three copies of money order receipts (stated to Ex.RW4/P1 be of his father), one copy of envelope (Colly) addressed to Rajesh Kumar from the police dated 31.10.2011, three copies of MTNL bills dated 16.01.2001, 09.02.2015 & 09.01.2015 in the name of Rajesh Kumar 2 Copy of letter written by his father dated Mark RW4/P2 PRAGATI 2026.02.11 01.07.1976 to PNB 3 Five original receipts (parchi) of various Ex.RW4/P3 organisations dated 24.08.2012, 18.04.2012, (Colly) 26.05.2012, 13.05.2012 & xxxx.12 (date not clear) He further stated that the business under the name and style of M/s Muradabadi Chicken Biryani Centre is being run from the tenanted premises since the year 2000 and Riyasat is looking after the said business since the year 2000 till date. That he has a license from the concerned department for running the said business in the tenanted premises. However, he was unable to identify the license from the record as he cannot properly read without his spectacles which he had not brought on the said date. He further stated that there is a license probably in the name of Riyasat issued by the department of Food Safety & Standards Authority of India, Govt. of Delhi, with respect to the tenanted premises. He volunteered that he had got the license made for Riyasat. He denied that he never remained in use and occupation of the tenanted premises in the capacity of a tenant or that respondent no. 5 is in use and occupation thereof as a sub tenant. He further denied that respondent no.5 is running the shop exclusively and he is in exclusive possession of the same as sub tenant. He denied that he has no physical control, supervision and possession over the tenanted premises and that he has no right title or interest in the tenanted premises. 12) The respondent No.4 also sought to examine another witness i.e. RW-2 Sh. Haafiz Riyasat (respondent no. 5) who tendered his affidavit Digitally signed by PRAGATI PRAGATI Date: 2026.02.11 18:30:41 +0530 Ex.RW2/A in his examination-in-chief. However, during the pendency of the trial, respondent no.4 expired and his legal heirs i.e. Ms. Nishi (wife) and Sh. Rohan (son) were impleaded as legal heirs of respondent no .4 vide order dated 28.07.2025. It was further submitted by learned counsel for respondent No.4 that after the death of respondent No.4, the aforesaid RW-2 was not in his contact. Thus, he never appeared before the court for his cross examination.
texts.arguments: That there is no such document wherein the petitioner has accepted him as her tenant qua the tenanted premises. 16) Section 14 (1) (b) of DRC Act as read as follows:- The Protection of tenant against eviction.-(1) Notwithstanding anything to the contrary contained in any other law or contract, no order or decree for the recovery of possession of any premises shall be made by any court or Controller in favour of the landlord against a tenant: Provided that the Controller may, on an application made to him in the prescribed manner, make an order for the recovery of possession of the premises on one or more of the following Digitally signed by PRAGATI PRAGATI Date: 2026.02.11 18:30:44 +0530 grounds only, namely:-(b) that the tenant has, on or after the 9th day of June, 1952, sub-let, assigned or otherwise parted with the possession of the whole or any part of the premises without obtaining the consent in writing of the landlord. 17) Hence, following essentials will be examined in the present case- i. Relationship of landlord and tenant exist between the parties. In the case of Bhairon Sahai (D) Through LRs. Vs. Bishamber Dayal (D) Through LRs. & Ors., Civil appeal no.9198 of 2017 decided on 18.07.2017 (relied upon by Ld. Counsel for the petitioner) it was found that the respondent no. 1 had parted with a portion of the (tenanted) premises in favour of respondent no. 2 without taking the consent of the appellant and thus, the respondents were directed to vacate the tenanted premises. 27)In the case of Prem Prakash Vs. Santosh Kumar Jain & Sons and Ors. (AIR 2017 SC 4060) (relied upon by Ld. Counsel for the petitioner), it has been observed as under:- Digitally signed by PRAGATI PRAGATI Date: 2026.02.11 18:31:10 +0530 "Undoubtedly, the initial burden to prove that the sub-tenant is in exclusive possession of the property is on the owner, however, the onus to prove the exclusive possession of the sub tenant is that of preponderance of probability only and he has to prove the same prima facie only and if he succeeds then the burden to rebut the same lies on the tenant." Urmila Thakur vs Anita And Ors on 11 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/158623517/ 14 28)In the case in hand, the petitioner has clearly established that it is respondent no. 5 who is in the possession of the tenanted premises and not respondents no. 1 to 4.
